objective: Prepare the existing planner for deterministic reuse with different domain skill catalogs while preserving Lunar behavior, contracts, authority boundaries, and rollback safety.
non_goals: rename lunar_planner or lunar.planner schema identifiers
split the distribution before a second-domain proof
rewrite the staged router or public entrypoint
create a second parser, router, workflow language, catalog, or executor
rewrite stored plans, continuations, or profiles

todos.action: Publish a checked coupling inventory classifying every embedded rule and resource as kernel, host adapter, domain policy, artifact-family policy, or compatibility contract.
acceptance: entrypoint, staged routing, ports, archetypes, provider families, external providers, report inheritance, contracts, profiles, schemas, facade, and release tooling are covered
each coupling has an extraction seam, risk, fixture owner, and rollback path
todos.example: Classify CAPABILITY_SIGNALS as Lunar vocabulary policy while keeping canonical digest calculation in the kernel.
todos.rollback: documentation-only; remove the inventory if inaccurate

todos.action: Freeze public APIs, signatures, exports, schema/profile versions and digests, receipt keys, enums, representative continuations, and canonical direct/new/extend/refine outputs.
acceptance: direct package and legacy facade baselines are stored
exact canonical JSON/bytes and a separately versioned semantic projection are stored
normalization is limited to enumerated timestamps and nonces
default receipt and continuation digests match exactly
field projections map normalized concepts to concrete versioned receipt paths
corpus covers BioConductor, Biomni, pharmaceutical routing, report inheritance, direct/control paths, typed gaps, and refinement
baseline distributions record median and p95 latency, peak memory, and canonical artifact size
no request causes execution or network access
todos.example: Project selected_target, selected_targets, adjudication candidates, requirement-ledger rows, and continuation validation through one versioned parity projection without hiding canonical serialization changes.
todos.rollback: fixtures are additive and do not alter runtime

todos.action: Define kernel invariants and extension threats before creating extension points.
acceptance: covers authority escalation, executable pack loading, traversal, descriptor collision, alias cycles, policy conflict, nondeterminism, and cross-request leakage
states that lower policies can narrow but never widen authority
todos.example: A domain pack requesting network authority is rejected even when its profile requests it.
todos.rollback: documentation-only

todos.action: Define an allowed-difference, versioning, deprecation, and rollback policy.
acceptance: authoritative equality fields and canonical default digests have zero tolerance
additive namespaced diagnostics are the only initial allowed difference
intentional safety hardening is isolated into a separately versioned change and cannot be mixed into a parity release
old stored state is never automatically rewritten
unsupported major versions produce typed blockers
todos.example: Bundle diagnostics may be emitted in opt-in mode but cannot reorder selected candidates.
todos.rollback: retain legacy behavior as the normative oracle

todos.action: Specify versioned planner-bundle, policy-pack, bundle-resolution-receipt, and capability-descriptor-v2 contracts without activating them.
acceptance: contracts include identity, compatible kernel range, resources, profiles, admitted scopes, domain policy, explicit host-governance policy, trust policy, and symbolic provider-binding references
host policy and every registry binding identity/version are digest-bound and provenance-visible
fixtures cover missing resource, duplicate identity, bad path, unknown required policy, and incompatible major
module strings, file paths, entry points, arbitrary import strings, and executable payloads are rejected as policy bindings
todos.example: A minimal bundle with a custom owner scope validates only when that scope is explicitly admitted.
todos.rollback: do not register or consume the new contracts

todos.action: Implement a pure, deterministic validator and resolver for immutable bundles.
acceptance: identical inputs produce identical ordered output and digest
symbolic bindings resolve only through a caller-constructed allowlisted registry
resolution performs no network access, plugin discovery, dynamic import, or unconstrained filesystem search
policy precedence is kernel then host then domain then profile then request
monotone narrowing composes, widening blocks as an authority violation, and incomparable or same-layer disagreement blocks as a conflict
todos.example: A stricter lower claim ceiling composes; a looser one blocks; incompatible same-layer ceilings report both policies rather than choosing a winner.
todos.rollback: feature remains unreferenced by the public entrypoint

todos.action: Add an immutable per-request PlannerContext containing the resolved bundle, frozen binding/configuration snapshots, and explicit host governance/trust policy.
acceptance: context construction and identity are explicit and deterministic
bindings cannot mutate after construction
providers are request-local or declare and test thread safety
filesystem-backed inputs are captured as digest-bound snapshots rather than assumed immutable
existing global configuration remains available only through a compatibility adapter
todos.example: Two contexts can be constructed with different admitted scopes and binding digests; operational isolation is proven later by PDG-020.
todos.rollback: public entrypoint continues constructing and using the legacy global context

todos.action: Declare a packaged bioagents-default bundle that points to current profiles, resources, policies, and provider bindings without moving their implementations.
acceptance: the packaged manifest and packaged resources resolve syntactically under python -I
host-only resources and project-support owners are typed as deferred until supplied by an explicit Lunar host catalog
omitting a bundle still means bioagents-default
all current profile IDs and owners remain unchanged
todos.example: PROFILE_BY_MODE is initially referenced, not rewritten, by the default bundle.
todos.rollback: ignore the manifest and keep existing constants authoritative

todos.action: Add a new explicit-context entrypoint and thread context through internal APIs while leaving the existing public compatibility signature literally unchanged.
acceptance: old callers need no changes
every current_ports/current_config read and module cache is inventoried and contextualized
the explicit path never consults process globals and every cache key includes the context/bundle digest
compatibility mode preserves existing receipt shape and digests
shadow mode compares legacy and bundle decisions without affecting the returned plan
todos.example: configure_ports remains supported by the old entrypoint while the explicit entrypoint bypasses globals in external sources, package providers, store, owner resolution, domain routing, archetypes, and report inheritance.
todos.rollback: request/context-scoped selection disables bundle resolution; an emergency default cannot mutate an existing context

todos.action: Move mode-to-profile lookup behind the default bundle using dual-read shadow comparison.
acceptance: every route resolves the same logical profile ID
profile bytes and digests remain unchanged
mismatch blocks promotion
todos.example: new_workflow continues selecting planner-resource://profiles/new-workflow.yaml.
todos.rollback: restore PROFILE_BY_MODE as the sole reader

todos.action: Move capability signals and semantic ranking adjustments into ordered, schema-validated Lunar vocabulary rules.
acceptance: fixed and mutation corpora preserve evidence hits and candidate order
each score change records rule ID and reason
exact component-ID exceptions remain explicit compatibility rules
todos.example: An oncology-manuscript rule remains Lunar policy instead of becoming a universal kernel heuristic.
todos.rollback: use embedded constants/functions

todos.action: Introduce a production capability-surface provider and move repository resource snapshots behind bundle declarations.
acceptance: in-memory hosts need no repository root
repository-backed Lunar receipts hash the same resources
missing optional resources are explicit
workflow and archetype ports participate in normalized surface construction
todos.example: A host supplies immutable capabilities/workflows/archetypes with schema and digest through one context.
todos.rollback: retain repository surface loading as LunarSurfaceProvider

todos.action: Add profile contract v2 with policy-declared catalog and owner scopes while continuing to accept every v1 Lunar profile unchanged.
acceptance: legacy fixed scopes and selected_package_skills_and_workflows remain valid
foreign scopes validate only when declared
undeclared or ambiguous owners fail closed
no schema ID is renamed
todos.example: software_assurance is legal in the demo bundle but rejected by bioagents-default.
todos.rollback: continue emitting and validating v1 only

todos.action: Convert family registry, decomposition, ordering, and quality tables into a Lunar provider-family policy pack consumed by the existing selector.
acceptance: normalized provider-family fixtures are byte-equivalent
generic selection imports no biomedical registry
unavailable families remain typed rather than substituted
todos.example: Biomedical multiomics decomposition stays in bioagents-default; another bundle defines its own families.
todos.rollback: restore FAMILY_REGISTRY as authoritative

todos.action: Place BioConductor, Biomni, and biomedical external-source activation behind named provider-catalog and source-planner bindings.
acceptance: Lunar preserves release pins, evidence ceilings, and no-execution posture
a bundle without these bindings neither imports nor mentions them
not-applicable and unavailable remain distinct
todos.example: A neutral request cannot trigger a Bioconductor package fallback.
todos.rollback: default bundle delegates to current modules directly

todos.action: Register controlled scientific report/paper inheritance as a Lunar artifact-family blueprint rather than a universal assumption.
acceptance: Lunar report requests inherit identical methodological controls and critiques
a foreign domain can bind a different controlled-deliverable blueprint
absence of a blueprint never activates scientific-report defaults
todos.example: An assurance report inherits traceable vulnerability evidence controls, not biomedical claim controls.
todos.rollback: keep current report_inheritance call in the default path

todos.action: Move specialized pharmaceutical route identifiers and domain planners into explicit registrations with deterministic activation and conflict rules.
acceptance: current pharmaceutical cases remain equivalent
registrations declare priority, evidence, compatible modes, and authority
ambiguous activations block with local repair
todos.example: Two matching domain planners yield a typed adjudication request, never last registration wins.
todos.rollback: restore embedded route keys

todos.action: Defer arbitrary profile-DAG overlays; define only safe predeclared extension slots and fully resolved foreign profiles.
acceptance: blocking controls attach only through a stable extension-aggregation node already dominating release
post-release additions are advisory only
single output producers, declared root inputs, release dominance, terminal/failure reachability, stable stage identity/order, and no gate bypass are validated
stage replacement, dependency deletion, authority relaxation, input/consumer mutation, output shadowing, and owner ambiguity are rejected
until these checks pass, the demo uses fully resolved profiles
todos.example: A new blocking quality stage is legal only when the base profile already routes release through the declared aggregation slot.
todos.rollback: use only fully resolved checked-in profiles

todos.action: Build a fixture-only software-assurance-demo bundle and surface with a distinct scope, vocabulary, archetypes, provider family, artifact blueprint, and five to twelve capabilities.
acceptance: bundle needs no kernel edits
request planning covers direct/new/extend/refine journeys plus at least one non-report journey
empty/minimal catalogs, renamed logical IDs, missing policy, and lexical-collision negatives are covered
typed gaps, provenance, generic claim calibration, evidence policy, and deterministic ordering remain active
todos.example: Plan an SBOM-to-vulnerability-to-remediation-to-assurance-report workflow.
todos.rollback: fixture remains test-only and can be removed without production migration

todos.action: Prove zero cross-domain leakage sequentially and concurrently.
acceptance: Lunar to demo to Lunar preserves original results
no candidates, vocabulary, profiles, sources, policies, audiences, Lunar-specific claim ceilings, or cache entries cross contexts
thread and asyncio interleavings, re-entry, provider exception, cancellation, teardown, and import-order permutations are deterministic and isolated
instrumented accessors prove explicit-context requests never call globals
all caches include context/bundle digest keys
todos.example: A logistics or assurance request never sees genes, cohorts, oncology, manuscripts, Bioconductor, or Biomni, while generic evidence calibration remains enabled.
todos.rollback: disable explicit multi-context use and retain default context

todos.action: Add mutation tests for descriptors, bundles, policies, providers, schemas, and aliases.
acceptance: reject duplicate IDs, alias cycles, traversal, unsupported majors, conflicting ceilings, undeclared providers, executable payloads, and authority relaxation
permutations preserve results only for collections declared unordered
profile stages, precedence lists, and ranking rules are tested as order-sensitive
provider exceptions follow the frozen legacy policy during parity; any fail-closed hardening is separately versioned
todos.example: A descriptor renamed behind an alias cannot silently inherit the old descriptor's semantic contract.
todos.rollback: tests are additive

todos.action: Register schemas for all public receipts and test old/new reader-writer combinations, additive fields, continuations, and persisted plans.
acceptance: current receipt constants have portable schemas
strict readers reject unknown majors
v1 readers ignore additive sidecars
read-modify-write actors preserve unknown fields wherever the contract promises round-trip preservation
actual pinned old-wheel/new-host and new-wheel/old-v1-facade subprocess tests pass
an old binary reads candidate-written legacy-v1 state
old continuations and stored plans remain readable
todos.example: A separately versioned bundle resolution receipt accompanies an unchanged v1 planning receipt and is mandatory for authoritative bundle-backed continuations.
todos.rollback: continue using current receipt versions; do not rewrite stored data

todos.action: Extend isolated distribution verification to wheel and sdist, manifest-discovered resources, and a host-provided neutral surface.
acceptance: wheel and sdist-built artifacts install in separate fresh environments and plan under python -I
builds originate from a clean tracked export with pinned build backend/tool versions and normalized archive metadata
no egg-info, cache, checkout path, or undeclared module contaminates artifacts
content manifests and dependency metadata match allowlists
offline installation from a prebuilt dependency wheelhouse passes
checksums and build attestation bind source revision, backend, Python version, and bundle/resource digests
reproducible builds pass under fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
checks become mandatory blockers before PDG-029
todos.example: The neutral probe succeeds without catalog imports or a Lunar repository root.
todos.rollback: retain current wheel verifier while new checks mature

todos.action: Add supported Python/OS, pinned-old-host/candidate-planner, new-host-through-old-v1-facade, direct-package/facade, performance, and reproducibility gates.
acceptance: release tooling discovers profiles and schemas from manifests
supported Python and OS combinations are explicit
dependency floors are tested
facade/direct parity runs in fresh subprocesses in both import orders

budgets are fixed before implementation: normal-path p95 latency at most baseline plus 10 percent, canonical receipt size plus 5 percent, and peak memory plus 10 percent unless an ADR approves stricter measured values
shadow-path doubled work is measured separately
todos.example: The direct package must not pass only because the compatibility facade injected repository paths.
todos.rollback: mark unproven combinations unsupported rather than weakening gates

todos.action: Document the minimal host recipe: validate bundle, construct context, supply immutable catalogs/providers, run route-only planning, and persist only authorized artifacts.
acceptance: an external sample host works from the installed distribution and in-memory descriptors
recipe states authority, schema, version, digest, failure, and rollback obligations
no Lunar filesystem assumption appears in the neutral path
todos.example: A 20-line host fixture selects software-assurance-demo explicitly and receives a typed plan.
todos.rollback: documentation and sample remain experimental

todos.action: Run bundle-backed Lunar planning as an opt-in shadow and compare every authoritative field against the legacy path.
acceptance: zero unintended authoritative differences across tests and benchmarks
diagnostic differences are namespaced and allowlisted
shadow execution has a separately budgeted latency and cannot alter returned plans
candidate bundle/policy/binding digests are emitted in a versioned binding receipt without changing legacy plan digests
todos.example: A mismatch in candidate order blocks promotion even when final prose looks equivalent.
todos.rollback: disable the shadow feature switch

todos.action: Exercise a rollback drill and define stop conditions before any default switch.
acceptance: request/context-scoped selection and a pinned known-good artifact restore the legacy Lunar path
preparation remains dual-read but writes legacy v1 only
candidate-written v1 state is readable by the pinned old distribution
no stored plan is rewritten
old schema/profile resources remain available
safety, continuation, readability, parity, and leakage regressions trigger immediate rollback
todos.example: A simulated continuation incompatibility pins the attested known-good release and returns new requests to legacy routing without data conversion.
todos.rollback: this TODO defines and tests rollback itself

todos.action: Define independent compatibility streams for kernel API, ports, schemas, bundles, policy packs, and catalog snapshots.
acceptance: major/minor/patch rules are explicit for every stream

before promotion, every authoritative bundle-backed plan is persisted beside a mandatory binding receipt and continuation integrity covers its bundle, host-policy, domain-policy, registry-binding, and catalog digests
legacy plan/receipt digests remain unchanged
legacy facade support window is at least two minor releases before a removal proposal
todos.example: Adding an optional policy annotation is minor; changing authority semantics requires a major contract.
todos.rollback: retain current version while policy is reviewed

todos.action: Require a formal go/no-go review before making bundle-backed resolution the default.
acceptance: legacy parity, safety, domain isolation, mutation, compatibility, distribution, concurrency, and performance gates all pass
every accepted difference is documented
rollback owner and support window are named
todos.example: A passing second domain cannot compensate for one unreadable legacy continuation.
todos.rollback: no-go leaves the compatibility path unchanged

todos.action: Evaluate neutral naming or a core/domain package split only after two independent domains pass all gates and at least one external host demonstrates operational value.
acceptance: decision includes quantified value, import and schema compatibility, two independent bundle sources, migration and rollback plans
no static Lunar imports remain in the proposed kernel boundary
default recommendation remains no split unless evidence justifies it
todos.example: A package split is rejected if it only improves naming while increasing release and compatibility risk.
todos.rollback: keep one distribution with segregated bundle resources
